why:
The `set_flags` bits of `BakedBootConfig` -- one per field, meaning `baked-set` as distinct from `use the compiled default`. They exist because the blob is fixed-size and pointer-free (so a post-link tool can patch it in place), which rules out `Option`, and because the zero value of every field is a LEGAL value that must not be read as unset: domain 0 is a real domain (the whole reason `c:get_default_domain_id` in the init stage carries the `NROS_DOMAIN_ID_INHERIT`/`NROS_DOMAIN_ID_EXPLICIT_ZERO` sentinels, issues 0206/0227), and the empty locator is the established `absent -- let the backend discover` value (issue 0330), not a missing one. A separate presence bit is the only encoding that survives both. ROS 2 needs none of it: absence of an env var IS the unset marker there. NOTE the C header defines the same four as `NROS_BOOT_SET_*` object-like macros, which the C surface extractor does not see -- these read as Rust-only in the report and are not.

RE-READ (phase-444 gap re-read, 2026-09-23) — `rust:BOOT_SET_NAMESPACE` had its own row carved out of this family as a `gap` + `adopt`, on the grounds that the bit existed and NOTHING SET IT. All three legs of that reason are now false and the row is DELETED, so the bit reads as the `extension` its three siblings always were. Measured 2026-09-23: the C/C++ emitter bakes a declared namespace and sets the bit, with a test guarding both directions (`packages/cli/nros-cli-core/src/codegen/entry/mod.rs`); `EnvRung` carries `namespace: Option<&'a str>` resolved `env > baked > ""` from `$NROS_NODE_NAMESPACE` (issue 0794, `nros-node/src/executor/types.rs:614`, `:704`); and the last leg — `nros::main!` passing an unconditional `None` as `BakedBootConfig::new`'s fourth argument — closed with issue 1410, now `status: resolved` and archived: `baked_namespace` (`main_macro.rs:3031`) computes it from the node's FQN and `boot_config_static_tokens` (`:3049`, called at `:1431`) emits it, with `baked_boot_config_namespace_tests` asserting on the EMITTED TOKENS rather than on the rule, because 1410 was a value that existed, was correct, and was never threaded into the call.
